card: Enables -Wmissing-declarations and -Wmissing-prototypes compiler warnings across the build system to catch undeclared global functions and divergent signatures. It cleans up 124 files by marking translation-unit local functions static, fixing mismatched declarations, and pruning unused declarations. It depends on PR 36744 and upstream changes to libmultiprocess, and contains temporary unmergeable commits for external subtrees.
evidence: Commit 410843a684: "The header declared AddInputs(..., bool rbf), which was never defined, while the definition takes std::optional<bool> and has no declaration."
Commit 0ae6589244: "These were declared in fa6b061fc1 but never defined or used."
Commit 535a121415: "It was declared locally in guiutil.cpp, so the definition was never checked against the declaration."
problem: Functions defined without prior declarations or internal linkage risk exposing global symbols accidentally, leaving dead declarations behind, or allowing declaration and definition signatures to silently diverge without compiler warnings.

risk.why: Compiler flag additions and changing symbol linkage across the codebase could trigger build or link failures across varied toolchains and platform configurations.

scope_notes: Spans 124 files across almost every subsystem to add static qualifiers and include headers. Contains temporary [nomerge] commits for subtrees and external dependencies (leveldb, crc32c, libmultiprocess).
summary: Enables the -Wmissing-declarations (GCC) and -Wmissing-prototypes (Clang) compiler warning flags in the build system. To satisfy the new warnings, it marks translation-unit local functions as static, fixes mismatched or missing header declarations, and includes placeholder adjustments for external subtrees.
uncertainties: No diff was provided; exact build system configuration and scope of subtree modifications cannot be verified directly.
